## Observed Facts
- Data Scope: BGL, 2005-06-03 to 2006-01-04 (the full corpus range [E2]), filtered to level = FATAL. That gives 855,195 FATAL Log Entries [E1].
- The Components with the most FATAL Log Entries are:
  - KERNEL: 626,450 Log Entries [E1]
  - APP: 228,536 Log Entries [E1]
  - LINKCARD: 206 Log Entries [E1]
  - MMCS: 3 Log Entries [E1]
- KERNEL and APP together account for nearly all FATAL Log Entries. These are Log Entry counts, not incidents.
- The tools return no Team or owner field. The BGL columns available are alert_tag, component, level and node [E2].

## Hypotheses
- Ownership probably follows the subsystem. A kernel/OS team might own KERNEL, an application or job-runtime team APP, a hardware or service team LINKCARD, and a control-system team MMCS. This is a guess from the component names, not something the logs show.

## Unknowns
- Which Team owns each Component. The logs don't contain a Component-to-Team mapping, so I can't name the Teams.
- Whether the FATAL volume is a few bursts or a steady recurrence. I haven't run a trend yet.

## Next Step
- Get the Component-to-Team mapping from a service catalog or on-call roster. Send KERNEL and APP first, since they hold nearly all FATAL Log Entries.
- I can also run a monthly trend of FATAL Log Entries for KERNEL and APP to show whether they recur or come in spikes.
